cluster_summary: Calling IsValid inside CommandResponseFromJSON turns the previously lenient integration decoder into a hard gate, so payloads that were tolerated before (unrecognized or differently-cased response_type, oversized ephemeral text) now fail the whole command with a 500/400 and lose all sibling content, an unannounced compatibility break with no config gate or deprecation.
rationale: Calling IsValid inside the decoder turns previously tolerated payloads into hard failures at both ingest sites (500 in DoCommandRequest, 400 in commandWebhook) with no config gate — the same compatibility-break concern the human thread raised when asking for a logged warning instead of an error.
thread_body: Let's not throw an hard error. This might break existing servers. Instead log a warning, similar to the caller of MessageAttachment.IsValid(). In general, we should use that method as a guideline.

cluster_summary: The two new AppError i18n IDs (model.command_response.is_valid.response_type.app_error and .text.app_error) are missing from server/i18n/en.json, so the raw dotted key becomes the error Message in logs, developer-mode responses and Go client errors.
rationale: grep of server/i18n/en.json finds no model.command_response.is_valid.* entries, so the raw id becomes the translated message; this is the human thread's request to run i18n-extract for the new error ids.
thread_body: These are new errors right? if so, please run make i18n-extract to add them to the i18n files.

cluster_summary: The text-length check compares len(o.Text) bytes against a hardcoded 65535 while the governing post limit is a configurable rune count (PostMessageMaxRunesV2 / determineMaxPostSize), so the two limits neither agree nor nest — CJK text is rejected that would fit, ASCII passes that fails downstream, and enlarged-column installs get a new fixed ceiling.
rationale: len(o.Text) counts bytes against a hardcoded 65535 while Post.IsValid enforces a configurable rune count (PostMessageMaxRunesV2 / determineMaxPostSize), which is exactly the byte-vs-character concern the human thread raised.

cluster_summary: Validation lives in the shared bidirectional decoder CommandResponseFromJSON, which Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam also use to decode server-emitted responses that are never validated server-side (plugin/built-in commands), so a response the webapp renders fine fails to decode in mmctl and every Go client; validation belongs at the ingest sites, not the decoder.
rationale: CommandResponseFromJSON is also the decoder used by Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam for server-emitted responses that are never run through IsValid server-side, so placing validation in the shared decoder is misplaced; the human thread asks for the same relocation of the call to commandWebhook/DoCommandRequest, albeit motivated by logger context rather than client breakage.
thread_body:

cluster_summary: IsValid recurses through all ExtraResponses and propagates any nested failure, so one bad extra entry (even at a depth no consumer ever reads) rejects the whole payload and discards the valid main message, contradicting HandleCommandResponse's per-entry tolerance.
rationale: One invalid nested entry (even at depth 2, which HandleCommandResponse never reads) rejects the entire payload with a hard error, contrasting with HandleCommandResponse's per-entry continue-and-log; this is a facet of the human thread's objection to hard-erroring instead of logging a warning.
thread_body: Let's not throw an hard error. This might break existing servers. Instead log a warning, similar to the caller of MessageAttachment.IsValid(). In general, we should use that method as a guideline.

cluster_summary: Validation is welded into the deserializer itself, unlike every other *FromJSON in the package (and unlike the structural sibling OutgoingWebhookResponse, which has no IsValid at all), so callers lose the ability to parse first and decide about validity separately.
rationale: Same defect as the maintainer's "let's not throw a hard error, this might break existing servers" comment on that exact return: validation is welded into the decoder so callers cannot parse and then decide, and the fix (move it out of FromJSON) is what the thread asks for.
